problems.statement: ED nurse understaffing is the cause of the ED length-of-stay rise (the client's explanation).
The LOS rise is almost entirely a boarding problem: admitted patients wait in the ED for inpatient beds (about 3.0 of the 3.2 h increase), while work-up time and treat-and-release times barely moved.
The March 2026 hospitalist rounding change (09:30 start, new admissions first) pushed medical-ward discharges later, delaying bed availability and driving ED boarding.
Overall inpatient capacity or demand growth (volume, acuity, occupancy, inpatient LOS) explains the boarding.
The ED nurses' workload, morale and walkouts are real, but they are mostly a downstream effect of boarding. Nurses are caring for inpatients in ED rooms and rooms are not available for new arrivals.

Discontinuing the APP provider-in-triage shift (May 2026) contributes to the worse door-to-provider time and left-without-being-seen rate, which are front-end problems separate from admitted-patient LOS.
The September cut in evening bed-cleaning staff (6 to 4) may be adding to afternoon and evening bed turnaround delays and boarding, but no turnaround data exist after June.
Funding the travel nurses by deferring medical-ward case manager hires, and pausing the 4 West huddle, would worsen the root cause.

actions.action: Scale the discharge-planning huddle (likely discharges seen first, orders before noon) to all four medical wards, and train all hospitalists in the protocol, keeping the 08:00 teaching meeting and 09:30 start.
actions.rationale: It targets the mechanism that produces boarding, and the pilot with schedule-assigned days showed 2.3 h vs 4.6 h boarding with comparable days and no spillover.

actions.action: Negotiate with the hospitalist group on discharge-first rounding or a split rounding structure that preserves the benefits they wanted (less early workload, teaching), with the Medical Director and CMO involved.
actions.rationale: The rounding rule is the upstream cause, and the hospitalists' retention concern means the solution must be a compromise rather than a return to the 07:00 start.

actions.action: Continue the 4 West huddle and do not float its charge nurse to the ED.
actions.rationale: The huddle is the only demonstrated fix, and pausing it would remove the benefit for a small and temporary staffing gain.

actions.action: Approve the $1.46M eight travel-nurse contract as the answer to the LOS problem.
actions.rationale: Staffing is at or above grid, with flat hours per visit and falling vacancies, so nurses would not remove the boarding that accounts for about 3.0 h of the rise.

actions.action: Fund the travel nurses by deferring the two medical-ward case manager hires.
actions.rationale: Case managers support the discharge process that drives boarding, and coverage is already below target.

actions.action: Run an ED-level interim measure such as an inpatient-boarder nursing model or surge protocol for afternoons, at modest scale and time-limited.
actions.rationale: It relieves ED nurses without addressing the cause, so it can be a short-term bridge while discharge timing is fixed.

actions.action: Review restoring the APP provider-in-triage shift and the evening bed-cleaning staffing once their effects can be measured.
actions.rationale: Their contribution is unmeasured: front-end metrics are quarterly only and no turnaround data exist after June.

actions.action: Present the board with a boarding and discharge-timing measure alongside the headline LOS, and reframe the nurse-staffing case as downstream.
actions.rationale: It points governance at the real driver and avoids committing money to the wrong cause.

nextEvidence: Bed-turnaround (discharge departure to bed clean/ready to ED patient placed) and bed-assignment delay data by hour and unit since July, with EVS reporting restored, to measure the September evening cleaning cut's contribution.
Monthly and hourly front-end series (door-to-provider, left-without-being-seen) before and after 1 May, to separate the APP-in-triage discontinuation from boarding effects.
Hospitalist-level and ward-level discharge timing and boarding for all medical wards under a wider huddle rollout, including whether the effect holds when all hospitalists use the protocol.
output.summary: The rise in admitted-patient ED length of stay is mainly boarding, not ED nurse shortage. Boarding accounts for about 3.0 of the 3.2 h increase, and ED nurse hours per visit, vacancies and grid coverage are flat or better. The timing matches the March 2026 hospitalist rounding change, which pushed medical-ward discharges later. A pilot on schedule-assigned days nearly halved boarding. ED nurse strain is largely a consequence of boarding. The travel-nurse contract and deferring case managers would miss or worsen the cause. Scale the discharge huddle and renegotiate rounding. APP triage and evening cleaning cuts remain unmeasured.
